propositions: The byte-equivalence oracle executes both production and legacy Pandoc subprocesses on all 884 corpus units, with the legacy process configured by shared mutable production constants, causing coupled comparison instead of independent validation.

Changing _PANDOC_TO from html to plain alters both production and legacy output identically, causing the oracle to pass despite the production behavior drift, proving the legacy subprocess is not an independent expected output.
The copied legacy Pandoc subprocess invocation adds 884 subprocesses and ~33 seconds to test runtime without providing independent verification of byte equivalence.

Cross-platform CI (macOS arm64, Ubuntu x86_64) receives a single Pandoc binary fingerprint in the fixture schema, causing rejection on platforms with different binary hashes despite identical version and output behavior.

Golden immutable fixture with platform-keyed binary fingerprint map and deterministic regeneration command replaces the copied oracle while preserving all 884 real production Pandoc calls and independent byte-equivalence assertion.

Implementation requires schema v2 supporting multiple platform/architecture fingerprints, stable platform selection, version mismatch detection, and regeneration validation to prevent silent drift on future Pandoc version or platform changes.
